blocks.text: HOARDING CLEANOUT FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions About Hoarding Cleanouts in King City

items.q: How much does a hoarding cleanout cost in King City?
a: Pricing is based on how many rooms or structures are affected — never on the address or the property’s overall value. The figure is confirmed free at a private walkthrough.

Completely, by design. Arrival times arrange around your schedule, nothing is staged where the road can see it, and no client’s situation is discussed with anyone outside the job — regardless of who’s involved.

items.q: Does a larger estate cost more than a smaller village home?
a: No. The price reflects the actual scope of the work — rooms, structures, sorting required — never the size or value of the property itself.

items.q: Can the cleanout include a barn or outbuilding on a horse property?
a: Yes — it’s regular work for us on King City’s larger properties. Crews work calmly around animals and active operations, and the whole property gets scoped and quoted together.

items.q: What's the best way to clean out a hoarder's house?
a: Professional help, a clear plan, and patience. Going in without a strategy usually causes more distress than progress. The most effective approach sorts systematically — keep, donate, recycle, dispose — and moves at a pace the household can genuinely handle.

items.q: What happens if we find valuables, documents or sentimental items?
a: They’re set aside immediately and brought to the family, never sorted into a donation or disposal pile by default.

items.q: What if the property has safety hazards — pests, mould, structural damage?
a: Those get flagged honestly. Live Junk Free doesn’t disturb suspected biohazards or structural issues — the concern is identified and the household is pointed toward the right licensed specialist before the rest of the cleanout proceeds.

items.q: Can you coordinate with an executor who isn't local?
a: Regularly. Photos, written confirmation of what was done, and documentation for the estate file are all available without anyone needing to be on site — shared only with the people who are meant to see them.
